turns.speaker: Gwendolen
turns.text: Mother, surely the address in Belgrave Square is of no consequence. Jack has a charming country home, and I do not believe one’s worth is measured by a London address.

turns.speaker: Lady Bracknell
turns.text: Gwendolen, I must remind you that in my experience, the address in Belgrave Square is indeed of the utmost consequence. It is the first test of a gentleman's true worth.

turns.speaker: Gwendolen
turns.text: Mother, you cannot possibly believe that such shallow metrics define a gentleman. Jack is a man of honor and integrity, and that is what truly matters.

turns.speaker: Lady Bracknell
turns.text: Gwendolen, I must insist that your perspective is overly simplistic. A gentleman's worth is indeed reflected in his social standing and his ability to provide a respectable home in London. Your father would agree with me.

turns.speaker: Gwendolen
turns.text: Mother, you dismiss my feelings so easily. Jack's character and the love we share are more important than any address or social standing.

turns.speaker: Lady Bracknell
turns.text: Gwendolen, I am disappointed in your lack of understanding regarding the importance of social standing. Jack must be able to provide for you in a manner befitting your status.

turns.speaker: Gwendolen
turns.text: Mother, your concerns seem to disregard the depth of my feelings for Jack. Love and character are more important to me than any address or status.

turns.speaker: Lady Bracknell
turns.text: Gwendolen, I must remind you that your father and I have high expectations for your future. Social standing is not to be taken lightly, and it is my duty to ensure that you marry well.

turns.speaker: Gwendolen
turns.text: Mother, I understand your concerns, but my heart cannot be swayed by social conventions. Jack is the man I love, and that is all that matters to me.

turns.speaker: Lady Bracknell
turns.text: Gwendolen, I understand your sentiments, but you must understand that I am responsible for ensuring your future security and happiness within the bounds of propriety and social convention. Jack, step forward and answer my questions.

turns.speaker: Gwendolen
turns.text: Mother, I appreciate your concern, but I must insist that you respect my choice. Jack is the man I wish to marry, regardless of your approval.

turns.speaker: Lady Bracknell
turns.text: Jack, I must ask you to address the matter of your address. Where are your parents? Your relatives? Your income?

turns.speaker: Jack
turns.text: Lady Bracknell, with all due respect, I can assure you that I am of good standing and have a respectable income. My circumstances may not be conventional, but I am committed to providing for and caring for Gwendolen.

turns.speaker: Lady Bracknell
turns.text: Jack, I must say that your assurances are not sufficient. Your origins are unclear, and that is a matter of considerable concern. Your income, while respectable, does not address the necessity of a clear and present family background.

turns.speaker: Gwendolen
turns.text: Mother, how can you be so unreasonable? Jack is a gentleman of character and integrity, and his income is more than adequate. I will not be swayed by your insistence on conventional origins.

turns.speaker: Lady Bracknell
turns.text: Gwendolen, your enthusiasm is commendable, but it is my duty to ensure that your choice is not made in haste or without due consideration. Jack, I am not unsympathetic to your situation, but the absence of a clear family history is a serious matter. I cannot condone such uncertainty.

turns.speaker: Gwendolen
turns.text: Mother, you cannot dismiss Jack so lightly. His character is what truly matters, not his past. I love him for who he is.

turns.speaker: Jack
turns.text: Lady Bracknell, I understand your concerns and respect your responsibilities as Gwendolen's mother. I am committed to providing a stable and loving future for her, and I hope you will consider my character and intentions beyond my background.

turns.speaker: Lady Bracknell
turns.text: Jack, your sentiments are well-meaning, but my duty as Gwendolen's mother requires a more thorough investigation of your past. I cannot overlook the lack of a clear family history and respectable lineage.

turns.speaker: Jack
turns.text: Lady Bracknell, I understand your position and I respect it. I will do everything in my power to provide the information you seek, to ensure Gwendolen's happiness and security.

opening.speaker: Gwendolen
opening.text: I am engaged to Mr. Worthing, mamma.

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: Pardon me, you are not engaged to any one. When you do become engaged to some one, I, or your father, will inform you of the fact. An engagement should come on a young girl as a surprise, pleasant or unpleasant, as the case may be. It is hardly a matter that she could be allowed to arrange for herself . . . And now I have a few questions to put to you, Mr. Worthing. While I am making these inquiries, you, Gwendolen, will wait for me below in the carriage.

opening.speaker: Gwendolen
opening.text: Mamma!

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: In the carriage, Gwendolen!

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: Gwendolen, the carriage!

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: You can take a seat, Mr. Worthing.

opening.speaker: Jack
opening.text: Thank you, Lady Bracknell, I prefer standing.

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: I feel bound to tell you that you are not down on my list of eligible young men, although I have the same list as the dear Duchess of Bolton has. We work together, in fact. However, I am quite ready to enter your name, should your answers be what a really affectionate mother requires. Do you smoke?

opening.speaker: Jack
opening.text: Well, yes, I must admit I smoke.

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: I am glad to hear it. A man should always have an occupation of some kind. There are far too many idle men in London as it is. How old are you?

opening.speaker: Jack
opening.text: Twenty-nine.

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: A very good age to be married at. I have always been of opinion that a man who desires to get married should know either everything or nothing. Which do you know?

opening.speaker: Jack
opening.text: I know nothing, Lady Bracknell.

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: I am pleased to hear it. I do not approve of anything that tampers with natural ignorance. Ignorance is like a delicate exotic fruit; touch it and the bloom is gone. The whole theory of modern education is radically unsound. Fortunately in England, at any rate, education produces no effect whatsoever. If it did, it would prove a serious danger to the upper classes, and probably lead to acts of violence in Grosvenor Square. What is your income?

opening.speaker: Jack
opening.text: Between seven and eight thousand a year.

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: In land, or in investments?

opening.speaker: Jack
opening.text: In investments, chiefly.

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: That is satisfactory. What between the duties expected of one during one’s lifetime, and the duties exacted from one after one’s death, land has ceased to be either a profit or a pleasure. It gives one position, and prevents one from keeping it up. That’s all that can be said about land.

opening.speaker: Jack
opening.text: I have a country house with some land, of course, attached to it, about fifteen hundred acres, I believe; but I dons depend on that for my real income. In fact, as far as I can make out, the poachers are the only people who make anything out of it.

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: A country house! How many bedrooms? Well, that point can be cleared up afterwards. You have a town house, I hope? A girl with a simple, unspoiled nature, like Gwendolen, could hardly be expected to reside in the country.

opening.speaker: Jack
opening.text: Well, I own a house in Belgrave Square, but it is let by the year to Lady Bloxham. Of course, I can get it back whenever I like, at six months’ notice.

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: Lady Bloxham? I don’t know her.

opening.speaker: Jack
opening.text: Oh, she goes about very little. She is a lady considerably advanced in years.

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: Ah, nowadays that is no guarantee of respectability of character. What number in Belgrave Square?
